summary: Wood-timber wartime lookout built c.1943 with Army funds in Grant County, WV; transferred to the state in 1948; listed gone; a 2011 USGS map labels the site.

facts.status_note: Listed as gone by the Forest Fire Lookout Association; no source says when it came down or what remains at the site
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service and State of West Virginia (register)

events.note: Built circa 1943 with US Army funds (register); c.1943 (Eastern US Lookouts)
Transferred to the State of West Virginia (register and Eastern US Lookouts); forest history gives 1944 and 1948 for the two wartime towers

evidence.supports: built circa 1943 with US Army funds to protect forest used for Army training
evidence.quote: This tower was built circa 1943 using US Army funds to protect portions of Monongahela National Forest used for Army training.

evidence.supports: transferred to the State of West Virginia in 1948
evidence.quote: It was transferred to the State of West Virginia in 1948.

evidence.supports: register lists USFS and State of West Virginia as administrators
evidence.quote: U.S. Forest Service and State of West Virginia

evidence.supports: Army funding paid for three temporary towers, c.1943; Pigeon Roost one of them; near Bismark on the Potomac Ranger District
evidence.quote: c.1943: Army funding was used to construct three temporary lookout towers for fire protection, one of which was the Pigeon Roost tower on the Potomac Ranger District near Bismark.
1948: The Pigeon Roost lookout was transferred to the State of West Virginia.

evidence.supports: forest history names two wartime towers built with military funds: Niges Cliff and Pigeon Roost
evidence.quote: Two other fire towers were built in 1943 and 1944 using military funds associated with the WVMA: Niges Cliff Tower and Pigeons Roost Tower.

evidence.supports: Pigeon Roost and Niges Cliff built entirely of wood timbers
evidence.quote: Niges Cliff, Pigeons Roost towers, were constructed entirely of wood timbers

evidence.supports: forest history gives 1944 and 1948 for the two towers without naming which
evidence.quote: The USDA Forest Service transferred ownership of these two fire towers to the State of West Virginia in 1944 and 1948.

evidence.supports: Army trained soldiers in the West Virginia Maneuver Area during the war
evidence.quote: the U.S. Army trained soldiers in the West Virginia Maneuver Area (WVMA)

evidence.supports: FFLA list shows the tower gone with its own coordinates
evidence.quote: Pigeon Roost Grant 39.18742 -79.22370 Tower Gone FFLOS US 1654, WV 45

evidence.supports: 2011 USGS topographic map labels a Pigeon Roost Lookout Tower near Pigeonroost
evidence.quote: From the Pigeon Roost Lookout Tower near Pigeonroost to the natural pass at Greenland Gap

evidence.supports: map is a USGS topographic map published 2011

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and Eastern US Lookouts both give 1948 for the Pigeon Roost transfer. The forest history's 1944 and 1948 pair for the two wartime towers does not say which tower went in which year, so it does not contradict 1948.

sources.title: Pigeon Roost Tower Site, Former Fire Lookout Sites register entry US 1654
Monongahela National Forest fire towers history (PDF)
2011 Map of Greenland Gap, Bismarck, WV

notes_for_editor: Two coordinate sets disagree: register N 39.185767 W 079.217394 versus FFLA 39.18742 -79.22370. The record's conflict note says they 'share a register number', which does not describe the disagreement; the disagreement is the coordinates, and this research does not decide between them. The 2011 map label shows only that the name was on a USGS topo, not that a structure stands. Eastern US Lookouts says three Army-funded towers while the forest history names two; flagged in the story. The register gives the transfer as 1948 and the forest history as 1944 and 1948 for the pair. Access, staffing and fire history: none in sources read. No photos found.
